headline: Greenlawn Cemetery water stays shut off until main breaks are repaired; casket-lowering policy talks continue.
summary: Two water main breaks have left Greenlawn Cemetery without water, and notices will be posted at all three gates. Staff are considering aeration units for the ponds, and the fountains will stay off until pond depths and infrastructure are fixed. Floating gardens are estimated at $2,600, but the current budget has no money for them.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 9, 2026 meeting, carried unanimously by roll call vote.
Continued the discussion of the casket-lowering policy until more information is obtained.
Agreed to target November for a hybrid meeting at the Community Life Center.

1 
 
 
 
DRAFT  
MINUTES OF THE CEMETERY COMMISSION 
AUGUST 11, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Cemetery Commission was held on August 11, 2026, at 6: 00 p.m., via 
ZOOM, an online video conference call system.  Present on call were Chairperson Jacob St. Louis, 
Members: Francis Murphy, Anthony O’Donnell, Zack Sanzone; Kieran Kavanaugh, 
Superintendent of Cemeteries; and Commission Clerk Joanne Roomey.   
1. Approve Cemetery Commission Meeting Minutes for June 9, 2026 
Mr. Murphy made a motion to approve the Cemetery Commission Minutes for the June 9, 
2026, meeting. Seconded by Mr. O’Donnell. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was 
carried unanimously.    
2. Public comment (limited to 15 minutes) 
• Polly Wilburt made a comment regarding what the commission was just speaking about.  
She said the legal case was in April 2019 in Lawrence at Bellevue Cemetery, when the 
lowering device straps snapped. She also commented about plant materials and if there 
were more prominent beds, that could tolerate the drought better. 
 
Jacob asked whether some of the grants are specifically designated for plants. Kieran 
confirmed that certain grant funds are used for this purpose. 
• Christine Lutts noted that the lack of water at the cemetery had been ongoing for over a 
week and suggested that, moving forward, notices regarding water shut offs be posted at 
the gates. She noted that many of the visitors to the cemetery are older indivi duals and 
felt it was important that notices be posted at all three gates indicating that there is no 
water.  
 
Kieran agreed and stated that notices would be posted at all three gates. Kieran explained that 
the situation was the result of two water main breaks. Kieran reported that there are currently 
two water main breaks at the cemetery. The cemetery has one main water shut-off valve. The 
water system is very old, and repairs are currently underway. The water had to be shut off, 
and notice of the shut -off was posted in the office. The water will remain shut off until the 
breaks can be repaired. 
 . 
 
 
DOMINICK PANGALLO 
MAYOR 
CITY OF SALEM 
MASSACHUSETTS 
CEMETERY COMMISSION 
57 ORNE STREET 
 SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS  01970 
TEL. (978)745-0195 
FAX (978) 741-7041 
 
 
JACOB ST. LOUIS, CHAIR 
 
BOARD MEMBERS 
 ANTHONY O’DONNELL  
FRANCIS MURPHY 
ZACK SANZONE
2 
 
• Mary Shalepoor made a comment. She is not from Salem  but loves G reenlawn 
Cemetery. There was a problem and she posted it on FB, and they told her to bring it 
here. She saw a bird covered with thick green growth on June 26th on the west side of 
Sargant pond. She has pictures showing the growth on the beak of the bird and all over 
its body, and she watched the bird struggle. It was dying and she wanted to help . She 
called the animal officer , the office, and tried to find someone at the funeral . She 
understands it is a man-made pond and the fountain is a problem, but she just felt awful 
seeing that poor bird and not being able to do anything about it. 
 
• Margaret Fleming  said under the agenda item of New Business has not seen any 
discussion of scattering of ashes at G reenlawn. She said it would n ot be that difficult 
to develop a policy around scattering of ashes.  
 
Jacob asked if she meant freely scattering ashes. He said he does not believe we have ever 
received any requests to freely scatter ashes.  
3. Kieran Kavanaugh Superintendent report about Cemetery Operations and Daily 
Operations report 
Greenlawn Cemetery 
• The Chapel Restoration Project is making good progress. 
• The West Chapel slope project has commenced, including demolition and disposal of 
materials. Staff provided a friendly reminder that the Martha Lyons Landscape Plan is 
being fully implemented as approved and reviewed by the Commission. 
• There is currently a water break due to the age of the cemetery’s water system. Two 
breaks have been identified for repair. Water service will remain shut off until the 
necessary repairs are completed. Visitors are encouraged to bring their own water, if 
possible. 
• Regarding wildlife concerns, visitors should contact Animal Control or an appropriate 
wildlife rescue organization. Cemetery staff are not equipped to handle wildlife  related 
issues. 
Charter Street 
• Zach reported that he met with Mary Richards regarding the property. Once the existing 
private fence is removed, staff will secure two small areas. The area will be secured to 
the extent reasonably possible, although it will not provide the same level of security as 
a full fence. 
• A cobblestone border is scheduled to be installed Thursday. 
• The property continues to experience good foot traffic. 
Friends Cemetery 
• The cemetery remains closed and locked. Regular maintenance continues. 
Howard Street Cemetery 
• The cemetery remains very quiet , with only occasional visitors.  Regular maintenance
3 
 
continues. 
Broad Street Cemetery 
• A meeting was held to discuss restoration of the damaged retaining wall. 
• Staff are finalizing the scope of work and funding requirements so the project can be put 
out to bid. 
• Although there is a list of other items that staff would like to repair, the retaining wall 
has quickly become the highest priority. 
Cemetery Ponds 
• Staff are working closely w ith the en gineering firm and contractors to develop and 
implement a solution for the cemetery ponds. 
• At this time, the fountains will not be returned until the pond depths are addressed, and 
necessary infrastructure repairs are completed. 
• Staff are considering the installation of an aeration unit at each pond. The units would 
circulate the water and promote a healthier pond environment and would serve as an 
alternative to the fountains. 
• An RDA is being considered for environmentally friendly treatments to address algae. 
 
4. Discussion around policy related to lowering caskets during internments 
Kieran gave a brief description of the current policies: 
• The lowering of caskets is a service typically provided through funeral service directors 
in connection with the purchase of a burial vault equipped with a casket -lowering 
device. 
• The cemetery contractors currently use a strap system and do not have casket -lowering 
services included in their contracts. They also do not have the required lowering device 
or specific liability coverage for this service listed on their Certificates of Insurance. 
• Potential changes to the policy may be considered moving forward. Any change would 
ultimately require the contract to be revised and put out to bid, which would likely result 
in increased costs. 
 
Francis raised the issue of families being permitted to witness the lowering of caskets during 
interments and spoke about the rules and regulations in Massachusetts. He noted that the issue 
has come before the Commission and that an updated policy is needed. 
The Commission discussed the importance of reviewing the applicable Massachusetts laws 
and regulations to ensure that the City's policy is consistent with those requirements. 
Jacob noted that witnessing the lowering of a casket is currently permitted under certain 
circumstances and explained  that liability is generally addressed through the respective 
contractor and funeral home. The discussion included potential liability involving the City, 
cemetery contractor, and funeral home. 
Kieran stated that the City can consider changing its policy, but any change would need to 
take into account available resources, equipment requirements, insurance coverage, and 
additional costs, which ultimately could affect residents.
4 
 
Kieran will include the issue as part of the Techra  Tech study and research the applicable 
requirements. Kieran will also work with the Assistant Solicitor to review and revise the 
policy for funeral homes and interments. The Commission will continue its discussion after 
additional information is obtained. 
Kieran noted that the City wants to ensure that any equipment used is appropriate and meets 
all safety and liability requirements. If the City ultimately determines that additional  
equipment or services are necessary, those requirements could potentially be incorporated into 
the specifications when the cemetery services contract is next put out to bid. 
5. General scheduling discussion for Cemetery Commission meetings 
Jacob inquired about the current meeting schedule, which is held on the second Tuesday of 
each month. The Commission discussed the possibility of occasionally meeting in person and 
agreed to target November for a hybrid meeting at the Community Life Center. 
6. Discussion around cemetery ponds including floating gardens, maintenance, and 
planned projects 
Kieran discussed shifting the floating garden item to New Business and suggested holding off 
on further action at this time. He acknowledged the algae issues and stated that a solution is 
being considered. 
Kieran explained that the existing water fountains will not be able to be returned to functional 
use, as they cannot be properly installed without likely breaking . The cost to repair the large 
fountain is approximately $7,000. 
As a new initiative, Kieran proposed installing an aeration system with a 60 -gallon pump to 
circulate the water. He stated that once the system is implemented, it should help address the 
issue. Kieran acknowledged that the current condition does not look good and thanked 
everyone for their patience. 
Kieran identified two issues that need to be addressed: (1) aeration and (2) the depth of the 
water. 
Zack asked whether the issue was related to the fountains that had turned green, noting that 
the fountain outside Village Tavern was particularly bright green. Kieran stated that he was 
unsure whether there was a connection. 
7. Continue the Dickson Chapel ADA discussion 
Jacob reported that the ADA plan had been presented to several other boards and 
commissions. He reviewed the minutes and noted that the feedback appeared to be favorable. 
Kieran provided an update, stating that the plan had gone before the various commissions and 
that the next step is to address funding. Determining how to fund the project is the final piece 
of the process. Several design options were discussed, including a  full glass door option and 
an option that would be partially boxed off. 
Jacob asked whether the plan would come before the Commission again. K ieran confirmed 
that it would, noting that this was only the first round of review and that there would be several 
additional rounds before the project comes to fruition.
5 
 
 
8. New Business:  
Floating Gardens  
Kieran reported that staff have been exploring options for two floating gardens at Greenlawn 
Cemetery. The proposed floating gardens would help reduce algae and increase oxygen in the 
water. The estimated cost is approximately $2,600. 
Kieran noted that the current Fiscal Year perpetual care budget does not have funding 
available for the project, as the existing funds are fully allocated. Staff will explore whether 
funding can be identified elsewhere. KK stated that, if necessary, a fundraising initiative could 
be considered, and he and his wife would be willing to assist with building the gardens and 
volunteering. He also has a meeting scheduled to determine whether funds may be available 
for the project. 
Jacob noted that the Commission had discussed the concept previously. He referenced a 
floating garden at Mack Park and indicated that there was a visual example available. Zack 
stated that he had no concerns with the concept and did not anticipate any issues, although he 
questioned whether algae could still be a concern with a floating garden. 
Anthony said he supported the idea provided that a plan is established for ongoing upkeep 
and maintenance. He questioned whether  maintaining the floating gardens would create an 
additional responsibility for cemetery staff and emphasized the need to identify who would 
be responsible for maintenance before moving forward. 
Kieran said he shared Anthony’s concerns and had discussed maintenance with Terry Bastian 
who indicated that the floating gardens would be self -sustaining and would not require 
significant maintenance. K ieran explained that the gardens would create a beneficial 
environment rather than contribute to existing issues. He noted that the cemetery has only five 
maintenance staff members responsible for five cemeteries, so the project could not become 
an additional s taff responsibility. Instead, maintenance and planting could potentially be 
supported through volunteers. 
Public Comment by Polly Wilburt: 
She said in FY19, the Community Preservation Committee (CPC) awarded a $35,000 grant 
for a study regarding the preservation of Broad Street, including funding for a consultant to 
prepare a report. She suggested that the Commission determine whether the report was 
completed and whether the Commissioners have reviewed its recommendations. 
She also said, because the CPC previously funded the preservation study, the 
recommendations contained in the report may provide a potential pathway for seeking 
additional CPC funding to implement eligible preservation or restoration work. She suggested 
consulting with Patty Kelleher regarding the process for submitting a subsequent grant 
application, particularly for projects that overlap with the preservation needs currently being 
identified by staff. She also noted that any proposed work would need to qualify as 
preservation or restoration rather than routine maintenance under the Community 
Preservation Act.
6 
 
8. Adjournment: Mr. Sanzone made a motion to adjourn. Seconded by Mr. St. Louis. A roll 
call vote was taken, and the motion was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 
7:25 p.m. 
Respectfully submitted,  
Joanne M. Roomey  
Commission Clerk
